subject: Zenith Health — urgent: elevated 5xx/429s affecting inference requests
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@zenithhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Zenith SRE Team <sre@zenithhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: High 5xx/429 rates since 07:40PT — production impacting

Karthik,

We started seeing a sharp rise in 5xx and 429 responses to our inference endpoints around 07:40 PT. Latency spikes and client timeouts followed — roughly 30% request failure rate and significant retry amplification from our side. This is affecting the live recommendation flow for 50% of users.

Attached a small request sample and logs (logs_zenith_20260611.zip). Can you confirm: 1) whether this is a Redwood-side infrastructure issue vs model-level overload, and 2) an ETA for mitigation? We are degrading traffic to a fallback but need a plan to stabilize.

Jordan
Senior Reliability Engineer
Zenith Health

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 rates since 07:40PT — production impacting

Jordan — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the logs. I'm escalating immediately. Initial read: symptoms look like request timeouts and upstream queue saturation leading to 429s plus downstream 5xx.

Immediate plan:
- I'm opening an internal incident and looping in SRE/engineers.
- Please continue routing to your fallback if useful; keep sampling traffic.
- We will post a short status update within 30 minutes and a technical ETA within 90 minutes.

I'll update in thread with internal owners. Apologies for the disruption — we know this is high impact.

Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: [Internal] Incident: Zenith Health — 5xx/429 spike (on-call)

Team — I'm taking on-call for this. TL;DR: sudden increase in per-inference tail latency causing upstream queue timeouts and 429s; we see correlated GPU worker CPU throttling and elevated kernel retries.

What I've done so far:
- Pulled the log bundle from Jordan and correlated with our ingress metrics.
- Scoped: affects gateway cluster rw-gw-us-west-2-2; model variant `gpt-transformer-v3-q8` appears frequently in samples.
- Kicked an administrative throttle to slow customer retries at the edge (temporary rate-limit) to reduce retry amplification.

Immediate asks:
- Diego: can you pull runtime kernel logs and check whether the quantized kernel path is experiencing OOMs or long GC stalls?
- Monica/Karthik: please coordinate the customer-facing short status update (30m).
- Evelyn: heads-up in case we need executive escalation/credits.

I'll push an A/B fallback to an older model variant (v3.1-nq) if kernel diagnostics indicate runtime stalls.

-Sean
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: mitigation_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook excerpt)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Internal] Incident: Zenith Health — 5xx/429 spike (on-call)

Sean — quick findings from runtime:
- We see kernel retries in the quantized GEMM path (q8) for the affected model; several workers reporting ephemeral kernel resource contention leading to >500ms tail latencies. No persistent OOMs but sporadic thread stalls when GC coincides with large batch windows.
- Ingress shows a 3x spike in concurrent active requests from Zenith between 07:35-07:50; they exceeded their expected traffic profile; client-side retries amplified load.

Recommended immediate mitigations (low-risk):
1) Zero-downtime fallback: route Zenith traffic to v3.1-nq (non-quantized variant) for their production route. This reduces tail latencies at the cost of ~20% CPU/GPU throughput efficiency.
2) Apply a short-lived admission control window (30s) to smooth spikes and drop pathological retries.
3) Roll a kernel micro-patch to delay GC during hot windows (will require careful rollout).

I'll start the fallback routing now and monitor. ETA for measurable reduction: ~8-12 minutes.

-Diego
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: mitigation in progress — routing to fallback variant, temporary rate-limit

Jordan — quick update: thank you for the log bundle. We have identified worker-side kernel contention on the quantized path and have initiated a zero-downtime fallback for your production route to `v3.1-nq`. We have also applied a short admission-control window at the edge to curb retry amplification.

What to expect now:
- Measurable drop in 5xx/429 within 10-15 minutes while we monitor.
- If you see any failures, please tag samples with "zenith-case-3421" and send to this thread.
- We'll follow up with a technical postmortem and recommended config changes (batching/quantization advice) after the incident.

I'll post a status link as well: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-06-12-zenith

Karthik

Karthik/Team — thanks for the fast action. We are seeing a large drop in errors and latency in our dashboards. 5xxs down from ~30% -> ~3% and 429s similarly reduced. Will continue to observe for the next hour; we'll keep retries disabled on our side for the time being.

Can you confirm whether Redwood will: 1) leave the fallback in place until the postmortem, or 2) move back to the quantized variant once kernel micro-patch is rolled? We want to coordinate planned cutover.

Jordan
